Definition: from G142; a number (as reckoned up):--number.
BiblicalUsage: Arithmos is simply a number, the count of something, and the New Testament counts people, crowds and signs with it. The believers grow to about five thousand men, five thousand sit down to be fed, a hundred and forty-four thousand are sealed, and John names the number of the beast as six hundred threescore and six.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe numbers in Scripture are never just numbers: they mark a people growing, a crowd fed, a remnant sealed, and a counterfeit counted. God numbers His own, and I hold that being counted among them is the only count that finally matters.
